entries.name: UNC Filename Support of File I/O VIs on Windows
entries.description: UNC filenames provide the primary means for specifying the location of a file or directory in a networked environment. In LabVIEW, you can enter and view UNC filenames in path controls, indicators, and constants in a file dialog box. UNC filenames use the following path form. \\<machine>\<share name>\<dir>\...\<file or dir> where <machine> is the name of the computer that you want to access on the network, <share name> is the name of a shared drive on that machine, <dir>\... consists of the name

entries.name: Tick Count (ms) Function
entries.description: Returns the value of the millisecond timer. The base reference time (millisecond zero) is undefined. That is, you cannot convert millisecond timer value to a real-world time or date. Be careful when you use this function in comparisons because the value of the millisecond timer wraps from Functions 1834 ni.com (2^32)–1 to 0.

terminals.name: millisecond timer value
terminals.description: millisecond timer value returns the value of the millisecond timer.

entries.name: High Resolution Relative Seconds
entries.description: Returns the relative current time in seconds. Use the difference between two successive values to measure the elapsed time between the calls. Use this VI to measure time spans with much higher resolution than you can obtain from the Tick Count (ms) function. The time resolution of this VI may vary with different operating systems and CPU types.

terminals.name: relative seconds
terminals.description: relative seconds returns the value of the second timer in seconds.

entries.name: Wait (ms) Function
entries.description: Waits the specified number of milliseconds and returns the value of the millisecond Note The operating system clock this VI uses is not tied to any absolute time reference and may drift over time when compared to absolute time sources. Avoid using this VI across long periods of time. Functions © National Instruments 1835 timer. (Windows) The actual wait time may be up to 1 ms shorter than the requested wait time. terminals.name: milliseconds to wait
terminals.description: milliseconds to wait specifies the number of milliseconds to wait. This function does not wait longer than 0x7ffffff or 2,147,483,647 ms or about 25 days. To wait for a longer period, execute the function multiple times or use the High Resolution Polling Wait function. Wiring a value of 0 to this parameter forces the current thread to yield control of the CPU.

terminals.name: millisecond timer value
terminals.description: millisecond timer value returns the value of the millisecond timer after the wait.

entries.name: Wait Until Next ms Multiple Function
entries.description: Waits until the value of the millisecond timer becomes a multiple of the specified millisecond multiple. Use this function to synchronize activities. You can call this function in a loop to control the loop execution rate. However, it is possible that the first loop period might be short. Wiring a value of 0 to the milliseconds multiple input forces the current thread to yield control of the CPU. This function makes asynchronous system calls, but the nodes themselves function synchronously. Ther

terminals.name: millisecond multiple
terminals.description: millisecond multiple is the input that specifies how many milliseconds lapse when the VI runs. Wiring a value of 0 to this parameter forces the current thread to yield control of the CPU.

terminals.name: millisecond timer value
terminals.description: millisecond timer value returns the value of the millisecond timer after the wait.

entries.name: Get Date/Time String Function
entries.description: Converts a timestamp value or a numeric value to a date and time string in the time zone configured for the computer. The function interprets timestamp and numeric values as the time-zone-independent number of seconds that have elapsed since Functions 1838 ni.com 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time.

terminals.name: date format (0)
terminals.description: date format selects the appearance of the date string . Date formats vary with your system configuration. To use a different date format, use the Format Date/Time String function. 0 short —1/21/94 1 long —Friday, January 21, 1994 2 abbreviated —Fri, Jan 21, 1994

terminals.name: time stamp
terminals.description: time stamp can be a timestamp or a numeric. If numeric, this number is the time-zone-independent number of seconds that have elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time [01-01-1904 00:00:00]. The default is the current date and time. If year is before 1904, time stamp is negative.

terminals.name: want seconds? (F)
terminals.description: want seconds? controls the display of seconds in the time string .

terminals.name: date string
terminals.description: date string is the string returned by the function according to the specified date format .

terminals.name: time string
terminals.description: time string returns the string formatted according to the configured time zone for your computer. want seconds? controls whether the string includes seconds.

entries.name: Stall Data Flow
entries.description: Delays the data flow of the wire for a specified period of time.

terminals.name: milliseconds to wait
terminals.description: milliseconds to wait specifies the number of milliseconds that this VI waits to continue the data flow.

terminals.name: value in
terminals.description: value in specifies the input value before the delay occurs. This input accepts any data type.

terminals.name: millisecond timer value
terminals.description: millisecond timer value returns the LabVIEW system time when the delay finishes.

terminals.name: value out
terminals.description: value out returns the value in value in .

entries.name: Date/Time To Seconds Function
entries.description: Creates a timestamp from a set of individual values that specify a date and time. Use the To Double Precision Float function to convert the timestamp value to a lower precision, floating-point number. The number is measured as the number of seconds that have elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time, assuming DST is set to 1. Functions 1840 ni.com

terminals.name: date time rec
terminals.description: date time rec is the date and time to convert. If is UTC is TRUE, date time rec is in Universal Time. If is UTC is FALSE, date time rec is in the configured time zone for the computer.

terminals.name: second
terminals.description: second can be from 0 to 59.

terminals.name: minute
terminals.description: minute can be from 0 to 59.

terminals.name: hour
terminals.description: hour can be from 0 to 23.

terminals.name: day of month
terminals.description: day of month can be from 1 to 31.

terminals.name: month
terminals.description: month can be from 1 to 12.

terminals.name: year
terminals.description: year can be from 1600 to 3000.

terminals.name: day of week
terminals.description: day of week can be from 1 to 7, which correspond to Sunday and Saturday, respectively. Note This function ignores day of week when building the timestamp.

terminals.name: day of year
terminals.description: day of year can be from 1 to 366. Note This function ignores day of year when building the timestamp.

terminals.name: DST
terminals.description: DST indicates whether the time is standard (0) or daylight savings time (1). You also can set DST to -1 to have the VI determine the correct time automatically each time you run the VI. If is UTC is TRUE, the function ignores the DST setting and uses Universal Time.

terminals.name: is UTC (F)
terminals.description: is UTC specifies if date time rec is in Universal Time or in the configured time zone for the computer. If TRUE, date time rec is in Universal Time. The default is FALSE.

terminals.name: time stamp
terminals.description: time stamp is the time that represents the date and time specified by the individual values in date time rec . If year and month are out of range, the results are unpredictable.

entries.name: Get Date/Time In Seconds Function
entries.description: Returns a timestamp of the current time. LabVIEW calculates this timestamp using the number of seconds elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time. Use the To Double Precision Float function to convert the timestamp value to a lower precision, floating-point number.

terminals.name: current time
terminals.description: current time returns a timestamp of the LabVIEW system time. LabVIEW calculates this timestamp using the number of seconds elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time [01-01-1904 00:00:00].

entries.name: Seconds To Date/Time Function
entries.description: Converts a timestamp value or a numeric value to a cluster of time values. This function loses fractional seconds of precision when converting the timestamp. If you convert date time rec back into a time stamp, the timestamp may not display the exactly correct value.

terminals.name: time stamp
terminals.description: time stamp can be a timestamp or a numeric. If numeric, this number is the time-zone-independent number of seconds that have elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time [01-01-1904 00:00:00]. The default is the current date and time. If year is before 1904, time stamp is negative.

terminals.name: to UTC (F)
terminals.description: to UTC specifies if date time rec is in Universal Time or in the configured time zone for the computer. If TRUE, date time rec is in Universal Time. The default is FALSE.

terminals.name: date time rec
terminals.description: date time rec returns the date and time. If to UTC is TRUE, date time rec is in Universal Time. If to UTC is FALSE, date time rec is in the configured time zone for the computer.

terminals.name: second
terminals.description: second is the number of complete seconds since the start of the minute. Values can be 0 to 59.

terminals.name: minute
terminals.description: minute is the number of complete minutes since the start of the hour. Values can be 0 to 59.

terminals.name: hour
terminals.description: hour is the number of complete hours since midnight. Values can be 0 to 23.

terminals.name: day of month
terminals.description: day of month can be 1 to 31.

terminals.name: month
terminals.description: month can be 1 to 12.

terminals.name: year
terminals.description: year can be from 1600 to 3000.

terminals.name: day of week
terminals.description: day of week can be 1 to 7, which correspond to Sunday and Saturday, respectively.

terminals.name: day of year
terminals.description: day of year can be 1 to 366.

terminals.name: DST
terminals.description: is DST returns a value for standard (0) or daylight saving time (1). If to UTC is TRUE, is DST is standard (0).

entries.name: To Time Stamp Function
entries.description: Converts a number to a timestamp.

terminals.name: number
terminals.description: number can be a scalar number, array or cluster of numbers, array of clusters of numbers, and so on, that represents the amount of seconds from the epoch time of 12 a.m., January 1, 1904 [01-01-1904 00:00:00].

terminals.name: time stamp
terminals.description: time stamp is a time-zone-independent number of seconds that have elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time [01-01-1904 00:00:00].

terminals.name: Tick Count(Ticks)
terminals.description: Returns the value of a free running counter at the time the VI wakes up. A free running counter rolls over when the counter reaches the maximum of Size of Internal Counter specified in the configuration dialog box.

entries.name: Time Delay
entries.description: Inserts a time delay into the calling VI. Dialog Box Options Option Description Time delay (seconds) Specifies how many seconds to delay running the calling VI. The default is 1.000.

terminals.name: Delay Time (s)
terminals.description: Specifies how many seconds to wait. The value you wire to this input overrides the value you set in the configuration dialog box.

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: Contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

entries.description: Indicates the amount of time that has elapsed since the specified start time. terminals.name: Reset
terminals.description: Controls the initialization of the internal state of the VI. The default is FALSE.

terminals.name: Time Target (s)
terminals.description: Specifies how much time must elapse before the Time has Elapsed Boolean is set to TRUE. The default is 1.

terminals.name: Auto Reset
terminals.description: Resets the start time to the value in Present (s) when the Express VI reaches the Time Target (s) .

terminals.name: Set Start Time (s)
terminals.description: Uses the current time or a time offset from 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904 [01-01-1904 00:00:00] as the start time instead of the time this VI first ran.

terminals.name: Present (s)
terminals.description: Displays the present time in seconds since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time [01-01-1904 00:00:00].

terminals.name: Start Time Text
terminals.description: If Automatically reset after time target is FALSE, displays (in text format) the date and time the VI first ran or the time you wire to the Set Start Time (s) input. Otherwise displays the date and time of the last reset.

terminals.name: Present Text
terminals.description: Displays the present date and time in text format.

terminals.name: Time has Elapsed
terminals.description: Indicates if the Elapsed Time (s) is greater than the start time plus Time Target (s) .

terminals.name: Get Start Time (s)
terminals.description: If Automatically reset after time target is FALSE, displays the date and time the VI first ran or the time you wire to the Set Start Time (s) input. Otherwise displays the date and time of the last reset.

terminals.name: error out
terminals.description: Contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.

terminals.name: Elapsed Time (s)
terminals.description: Displays the amount of time in seconds that has elapsed since the start time and the Present (s) time.

terminals.name: Elapsed Time Text
terminals.description: Displays the amount of time in seconds that has elapsed since the start time.

entries.description: Waits the specified number of seconds with higher resolution than you can obtain with the Wait (ms) function. For example, use this VI in applications that require waiting with sub-millisecond resolution between steps. The resolution of the timer this VI uses varies with different operating systems and CPU types. terminals.description: error in describes error conditions that occur before this node runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.

entries.name: Format Date/Time String Function
entries.description: Displays a timestamp value or a numeric value as time in the format you specify using time format codes.

terminals.name: time format string (%c)
terminals.description: time format string specifies the format of the output string. Time format codes (beginning with % ) not recognized by the function as a format code return the character literally. The default code is %c , which corresponds to the date/time representation appropriate for the configured time zone for the computer. If time format string is an empty string, the function uses the default.

terminals.name: time stamp
terminals.description: time stamp can be a timestamp or a numeric. If numeric, this number is the time-zone-independent number of seconds that have elapsed since 12:00 a.m., Friday, January 1, 1904, Universal Time [01-01-1904 00:00:00]. The default is the current date and time. If year is before 1904, time stamp is negative.

terminals.name: UTC format
terminals.description: UTC format specifies if the output string is in Universal Time or in the configured time zone for the computer. If TRUE, date/time string is in Universal Time. The default is FALSE.

terminals.name: date/time string
terminals.description: date/time string is the formatted date/time string.
